l: words of Christ, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 33
s: The words of Christ teach all men that they should do good. Christ will show with power and great glory at the last day whether the written words are his.

l: writing, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 33
s: Nephi's writing is done in weakness but will be made strong unto his readers. It makes known things about their fathers, speaks of Jesus, persuades people to believe in him, and speaks harshly against sin according to the plainness of truth.

l: prayers, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 33
s: Nephi prays continually for his people by day and weeps for them by night. He knows that the Lord God will consecrate his prayers for their gain.

l: sin, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 33
s: Nephi's writing speaks harshly against sin according to the plainness of the truth. He says no one will be angry at those words unless that person is of the spirit of the devil.

l: truth, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 33
s: Nephi glories in truth. His writing speaks against sin according to the plainness of the truth.

l: faith in Christ, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 33
s: Nephi has great faith in Christ that he will meet many souls spotless at Christ's judgment-seat. He also cries unto God in faith.

l: the narrow gate, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 33
s: People who are to be reconciled unto Christ must enter into the narrow gate.

l: straight and narrow path, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 33
s: The strait path leads to life, and those who enter it must continue in it until the end of the day of probation.

l: eternal life, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 33
s: Enduring to the end is identified as life eternal.

l: kingdom of God, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 33
s: Nephi prays the Father in the name of Christ that many, if not all, may be saved in God's kingdom at the great and last day.

l: the day of probation, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 33
s: Those who are reconciled unto Christ must continue in the strait path until the end of the day of probation.

l: judgment, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 33
s: At the final judgment, Christ will show that the words are his, and Nephi and his readers will stand face to face before Christ's bar. Those who reject the goodness of God, the words of the Jews, Nephi's words, and the words proceeding from the Lamb of God will be condemned.

l: The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi / Chapter 1
s: This unit concerns Jacob’s record of Nephi’s commandments about the small plates and the spiritual teachings to be preserved on them. Jacob and Joseph serve as consecrated priests and teachers, laboring to persuade the people of Nephi to come unto Christ and obey God. Nephi dies after appointing a successor, and the people continue naming their kings after him. Under the second king, the people begin to grow hard in their hearts, pursue wealth, and practice wickedness, including desiring many wives and concubines.

l: Jacob, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi / Chapter 1
s: Jacob receives commandments from Nephi to write precious spiritual teachings on the small plates and preserve them for his seed. He and Joseph are consecrated priests and teachers, and Jacob teaches the people of Nephi, urging them to come unto Christ and fulfill God’s commandments.

l: Nephi, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi / Chapter 1
s: Nephi commands Jacob concerning the small plates and the preservation of sacred preaching, revelation, and prophecy. He appoints a man as king and ruler over the people, then dies after the people have greatly loved and honored him.

l: Christ, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi / Chapter 1
s: Jacob and his people know of Christ through revelations and prophecy. Jacob labors to persuade all people to believe in Christ, view his death, bear his cross, and come unto him.

l: God, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi / Chapter 1
s: Jacob and his fellow teachers labor to persuade the people to come unto Christ and partake of God’s goodness. Jacob warns against rebelling against God and provoking him to anger.

l: people of Nephi, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi / Chapter 1
s: The people of Nephi are taught by Jacob and Joseph, who seek to persuade them to come unto Christ. Under the second king, they begin to grow hard in their hearts, pursue gold and silver, become proud, and indulge in wicked practices.

l: Nephites, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi / Chapter 1
s: The people friendly to Nephi are called Nephites, or the people of Nephi, according to the reigns of the kings. The term Nephites is also used for those who are not Lamanites.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi / Chapter 1
s: Jacob says he will call those who seek to destroy the people of Nephi Lamanites. He no longer distinguishes the groups by their former family names.

l: temple, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi / Chapter 1
s: Jacob teaches the people in the temple after obtaining his errand from the Lord.

l: small plates, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi / Chapter 1
s: Nephi commands Jacob to write on the small plates the things he considers most precious. Jacob is to preserve sacred preaching, great revelation, and prophecy on them and hand them down to his seed.

l: doctrine of Christ, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi / Chapter 1
s: The heading states that the unit concerns a man who seeks to overthrow the doctrine of Christ, and that Jacob confounds him.

l: Christ’s kingdom, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi / Chapter 1
s: Jacob and his people learn of Christ’s kingdom through revelations and the spirit of prophecy.

l: word of God, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi / Chapter 1
s: Jacob and Joseph are responsible for teaching the word of God with diligence. Jacob says that their labor protects them from having the people’s blood come upon their garments.

l: sin, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi / Chapter 1
s: Jacob and Joseph take responsibility for the sins of the people if they fail to teach the word of God diligently.

l: death of Nephi, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi / Chapter 1
s: Nephi dies after becoming old and appointing a man to be king and ruler over his people. The people retain his name in remembrance by calling succeeding rulers second Nephi, third Nephi, and so forth.

l: The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 2
s: Jacob speaks to the people of Nephi in the temple after Nephi's death, declaring the word of God and warning them about their sins. He condemns their pride, costly apparel, persecution of poorer brethren, and misuse of riches. He also declares that whoredoms and plural wives are abominable, and that the people must have one wife and keep the commandments. Jacob says their wickedness has wounded their wives and children and brought condemnation upon them.

l: Jacob, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 2
s: Jacob speaks to the people of Nephi in the temple after Nephi's death. He declares the word of God, admonishes the people for their crimes, and testifies concerning their pride, riches, and whoredoms.

l: Nephi, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 2
s: Nephi has died before Jacob speaks to the people of Nephi.

l: people of Nephi, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 2
s: The people of Nephi have obtained riches and begun to labor in sin. They are condemned for pride, persecution, whoredoms, and breaking the hearts of their wives and children.

l: God, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 2
s: God gives Jacob a strict commandment to declare the word to the people and condemns their pride, whoredoms, and abominations. God regards one being as precious as another and has created all flesh to keep his commandments and glorify him forever.

l: Christ, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 2
s: The people are taught to obtain a hope in Christ before seeking riches.

l: wives, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 2
s: The tender wives of the people are wounded because of their husbands' wickedness, and their hearts are broken by bad examples.

l: daughters of this people, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 2
s: The daughters of this people are fair and tender. God hears their cries and mourning and will not suffer the men to lead them away captive without visiting the men with a sore curse.

l: land of promise, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 2
s: The land of promise abounds plentifully in gold, silver, and all manner of precious ores.

l: word of God, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 2
s: The word of God is declared by Jacob according to God's command. It is described as pleasing and able to heal the wounded soul, but it also exposes wickedness and pierces delicate minds when people must be admonished.

l: commandments, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 2
s: The people have known the commandments given to Lehi but have done things they ought not to have done. They must keep the commandments or the land will be cursed for their sakes.

l: pride, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 2
s: Pride causes some people to lift up their hearts, wear costly apparel, and persecute their brethren because they suppose they are better than others. Jacob condemns this pride and warns that it can destroy their souls.

l: riches, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 2
s: The people obtain many riches from the land. They are taught to seek the kingdom of God before riches and, after obtaining a hope in Christ, to use riches to clothe the naked, feed the hungry, liberate the captive, and relieve the sick and afflicted.

l: sin, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 2
s: The people begin to labor in sin, which Jacob considers abominable before him and God. Their sins include pride, persecution, and sexual wrongdoing.

l: whoredoms, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 2
s: Whoredoms are an abomination before God. The men are commanded to have no concubines and not to commit whoredoms like those of old.

l: chastity, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 2
s: God delights in the chastity of women.

l: the kingdom of God, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 2
s: The people are commanded to seek the kingdom of God before seeking riches.

l: The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 3
s: Jacob speaks to the people of Nephi, urging the pure in heart to look to God, pray with faith, and receive comfort and justice. He warns the filthy that unless they repent, the land of their inheritance will be cursed, the Lamanites will scourge them, and the righteous will be led away. Jacob teaches that the Lamanites are more righteous in observing the commandment concerning marriage and warns the people of Nephi against reviling them, fornication, lasciviousness, and every kind of sin. He records that these plates are called the plates of Jacob and were made by the hand of Nephi.

l: Jacob, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 3
s: Jacob speaks to those who are pure in heart and urges them to look unto God, pray with exceeding faith, and receive the pleasing word of God. He warns the people of Nephi to repent, remember their own filthiness, and avoid reviling the Lamanites.

l: God, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 3
s: God consoles the pure in heart in their afflictions, pleads their cause, and sends down justice upon those who seek their destruction. God will not destroy the Lamanites because they observe the commandment concerning marriage and will be merciful unto them.

l: the pure in heart, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 3
s: The pure in heart are told to look unto God with firmness of mind and pray unto him with exceeding faith. They may receive the pleasing word of God, feast upon his love, and continue forever if their minds are firm.

l: the filthy, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 3
s: The filthy are warned that the land is cursed for their sakes unless they repent. They are told that the Lamanites will scourge them unto destruction and that the Lord God will lead away the righteous from among them.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 3
s: The Lamanites are described as brethren who are more righteous than the people of Nephi because they observe the commandment concerning marriage. Their husbands and wives love one another and their children, and one day they shall become a blessed people.

l: people of Nephi, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 3
s: The people of Nephi are warned against fornication, lasciviousness, and every kind of sin. They are told to remember their children, avoid reviling the Lamanites, and repent so that their children are not brought unto destruction.

l: the land of inheritance, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 3
s: The land of inheritance will be possessed by the Lamanites if the filthy do not repent. The Lord God will lead away the righteous from among those who remain.

l: the commandment concerning marriage, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 3
s: The commandment concerning marriage requires that there should be only one wife and no concubines, and that there should be no whoredoms. The Lamanites observe this commandment, and because of it the Lord God will not destroy them.

l: word of God, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 3
s: The pure in heart are told to lift up their heads and receive the pleasing word of God. They may feast upon it and upon God's love if their minds are firm.

l: God's love, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 3
s: The pure in heart are invited to feast upon God's love. They may do so forever if their minds are firm.

l: the cursing of the Lamanites, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 3
s: The Lamanites are described as having a sore cursing, which is connected to the cursing that has come upon their skins. Despite this cursing, they are not filthy like the people of Nephi and observe the commandment concerning marriage.

l: destruction, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 3
s: The Lamanites will scourge the filthy unto destruction if they do not repent. Filthiness may also bring the children of the people of Nephi unto destruction.

l: repentance, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 3
s: Repentance is required of the filthy to prevent the land from being cursed and the Lamanites from possessing the land of inheritance. Jacob warns that failure to repent will bring destruction and the loss of the righteous.

l: filthiness, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 3
s: Filthiness causes the land to be cursed and can bring children unto destruction. Jacob commands the people of Nephi to remember their own filthiness and not revile the Lamanites because of theirs.

l: sin, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 3
s: Jacob warns the people of Nephi against their sins, including fornication and lasciviousness. Their sins may be heaped upon their heads at the last day.

l: the darkness of their skins, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 3
s: The people of Nephi are commanded to revile no more against the Lamanites because of the darkness of their skins. They are told instead to remember their own filthiness.

l: the plates, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 3
s: The plates contain the proceedings of the people of Nephi, including their wars, contentions, and the reigns of their kings. A hundredth part of those proceedings cannot be written upon them.

l: the plates of Jacob, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 3
s: The plates of Jacob are made by the hand of Nephi. Jacob identifies them by this name at the end of his words.

l: The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 4
s: Jacob explains that he and his people engrave their words on plates so their children and brethren may learn about their fathers and their knowledge of Christ. He teaches that Christ, his atonement, resurrection, and glory were known and hoped for by Jacob, the holy prophets, and their fathers before Christ’s coming. Jacob warns against despising revelations or counseling God, and he prophesies that the Jews will reject the sure foundation but that the stone will become the head of the corner.

l: Jacob, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 4
s: Jacob says he has ministered to his people and writes on plates so their children and brethren may gain knowledge of their fathers. He teaches about Christ, the atonement, resurrection, revelations, and the sure foundation, and he is led by the Spirit to prophesy concerning the Jews.

l: Christ, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 4
s: Christ is identified as the one whose glory Jacob and the holy prophets hoped for before his coming. Christ is also described as the Only Begotten Son and as the stone upon which the Jews might build.

l: God, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 4
s: God reveals mysteries and his ways to humanity, and his word created the earth and man. He counsels in wisdom, justice, and mercy, shows weakness so that people know power comes by his grace, and gives people plainness or removes it according to their desires.

l: Jews, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 4
s: The Jews are described as stiffnecked, despising plain words, killing prophets, and seeking things they could not understand. Because they looked beyond the mark, they stumbled and rejected the sure foundation, though they may later build upon the stone.

l: prophets, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 4
s: The holy prophets before Jacob believed in Christ, worshiped the Father in Christ’s name, and hoped for Christ’s glory. Prophets of old also spoke of the things Jacob and others witness.

l: law of Moses, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 4
s: The law of Moses points souls to Christ and is kept by Jacob’s people. It is sanctified to them for righteousness, as obedience was accounted unto Abraham in offering Isaac.

l: atonement of Christ, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 4
s: The atonement of Christ is presented as the means by which people may be reconciled unto God. Through it, they may obtain a resurrection and be presented as the first-fruits of Christ unto God.

l: resurrection, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 4
s: Resurrection is associated with the power that is in Christ. Jacob teaches that people may attain knowledge of the resurrection and the world to come.

l: Spirit (God's spirit), The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 4
s: The Spirit provides revelations, prophecy, and understanding of things as they really are and will be. Jacob is led by the Spirit to prophesy, and the Spirit speaks truth and does not lie.

l: stone (sure foundation), The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 4
s: The stone is the great, last, and only sure foundation upon which the Jews can build. Although the Jews reject it, it will become the head of their corner.

l: foundation, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 4
s: A safe foundation is associated with the stone that the Jews reject. The stone is described as the only sure foundation upon which they can build.

l: faith, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 4
s: Faith becomes unshaken through searching the prophets, receiving revelations, and having the spirit of prophecy. Faith in Christ is included among the conditions for obtaining resurrection and hope of glory.

l: hope, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 4
s: Jacob and the holy prophets have hope of Christ’s glory before his coming. Through witnesses, faith, and knowledge of Christ, people obtain a hope of glory before Christ manifests himself in the flesh.

l: coming of Christ, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 4
s: Jacob’s people and the holy prophets knew of Christ and hoped for his glory many hundred years before his coming. Christ’s coming is described as his manifesting himself in the flesh.

l: The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 5
s: The Lord of the vineyard tends a tame olive-tree and grafts branches from a wild olive-tree into it to preserve its roots and fruit. The natural branches are planted in different parts of the vineyard, but over time the trees bring forth both good and evil fruit, and the vineyard becomes corrupt. The Lord of the vineyard and his servants prune, nourish, graft, and labor with their might until the natural fruit is restored and the bad branches are cast away. At the end, the Lord of the vineyard says that the vineyard will eventually be burned when the season and the end come.

l: house of Israel, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 5
s: The house of Israel is likened to a tame olive-tree that a man took, nourished, and planted in his vineyard. Its branches are pruned, grafted, scattered, and later gathered again as the natural fruit is restored.

l: the Lord, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 5
s: The Lord of the vineyard prunes, digs about, nourishes, grafts, and watches the trees in his vineyard. He preserves natural branches and roots, mourns when the trees become corrupt, spares the vineyard longer at the servant's request, and directs servants to restore the natural fruit and cast away the bad. He says that the good fruit will be preserved, the bad will be cast away, and the vineyard will eventually be burned.

l: servant of the Lord of the vineyard, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 5
s: The servant of the Lord of the vineyard carries out the Lord's commands by grafting branches, nourishing the trees, and laboring in the vineyard. He asks the Lord to spare the vineyard longer and explains that the branches have overcome the good roots. He later brings other servants to labor with him.

l: the vineyard, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 5
s: The vineyard contains a tame olive-tree, wild olive branches, natural branches planted in different places, and trees that produce both good and bad fruit. After extensive pruning, digging, nourishing, dunging, and grafting, the vineyard again produces natural fruit and is no longer corrupt. The Lord of the vineyard says it will ultimately be burned after the good and bad are gathered.

l: tame olive-tree, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 5
s: The tame olive-tree grows old and begins to decay, so the master prunes it, digs about it, and nourishes it. Its main branches are removed, wild olive branches are grafted in, and its natural branches are planted elsewhere. After further grafting and care, its natural fruit is restored.

l: wild olive-tree, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 5
s: Branches are taken from the wild olive-tree and grafted into the tame olive-tree in place of branches that are cast into the fire. The wild branches take strength from the roots and initially bring forth tame fruit, but later they overrun the roots and produce much evil fruit. Some wild branches are eventually removed, while others are retained and grafted according to the strength of the good branches.

l: natural tree, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 5
s: The natural tree and its branches are planted in different parts of the vineyard to preserve the natural branches and roots. Its natural branches later become wild and produce corrupt fruit, but branches are exchanged and grafted back into the mother tree. Through continued labor, the natural branches and roots regain strength and bring forth natural fruit.

l: The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 6
s: The speaker prophesies that Zenos’s words concerning the house of Israel, likened to a tame olive-tree, will come to pass. The Lord’s servants will again labor in the vineyard to nourish and prune it, after which the end will soon come, with the diligent blessed and the cast out cursed. The speaker urges my brethren to repent, cleave unto God, and not harden their hearts, warning that rejecting the prophets, Christ, and the good word of Christ brings shame before God and condemnation. The speaker calls them to enter the strait gate and continue in the way which is narrow until they obtain eternal life.

l: Jacob, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 6
s: The speaker prophesies concerning the house of Israel and urges my brethren to repent, cleave unto God, and not harden their hearts. The speaker warns of judgment for rejecting the words concerning Christ and bids farewell until meeting before the bar of God.

l: my brethren, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 6
s: My brethren are urged to repent, come with full purpose of heart, cleave unto God, and hear his voice without hardening their hearts. They are warned that rejecting the prophets, Christ, and the good word of Christ will bring shame and awful guilt before the bar of God.

l: house of Israel, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 6
s: The house of Israel is likened by Zenos to a tame olive-tree. The Lord remembers it, both roots and branches, and will recover his people.

l: the Lord, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 6
s: The Lord will set his hand again the second time to recover his people. His servants will go forth in his power to nourish and prune his vineyard.

l: servants of the Lord of the vineyard, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 6
s: The servants of the Lord will go forth in the Lord’s power to nourish and prune his vineyard at the last time.

l: the vineyard, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 6
s: The vineyard will be nourished and pruned by the servants of the Lord. Those who labor diligently in it will be blessed, while those cast out will be cursed and sent into their own place.

l: God, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 6
s: God remembers the house of Israel and stretches forth his hands unto them all the day long. Those who will not harden their hearts can be saved in the kingdom of God.

l: the kingdom of God, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 6
s: The kingdom of God is the place where those who will not harden their hearts can be saved.

l: mercy, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 6
s: God’s mercy is described as great, and his arm of mercy is extended toward my brethren in the light of the day.

l: repentance, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 6
s: Repentance is urged upon my brethren as they are called to come with full purpose of heart and cleave unto God.

l: the good word of God, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 6
s: The good word of God nourishes people all the day long. Those who bring forth evil fruit after being nourished must be hewn down and cast into the fire.

l: Christ, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 6
s: Many have spoken concerning Christ, and my brethren are warned not to reject the words concerning him or deny the good word of Christ.

l: the great plan of redemption, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 6
s: The great plan of redemption has been laid for my brethren. They are warned not to make a mock of it.

l: redemption, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 6
s: The power of redemption that is in Christ will bring those who reject the warnings to stand with shame and awful guilt before the bar of God.

l: resurrection, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 6
s: The power of the resurrection that is in Christ will bring those who reject the warnings to stand before the bar of God with shame and awful guilt.

l: justice, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 6
s: Justice cannot be denied. According to its power, those who reject the warnings must go away into the lake of fire and brimstone.

l: the lake of fire and brimstone, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 6
s: The lake of fire and brimstone has unquenchable flames and smoke that ascends forever and ever. Those condemned by justice must go away into it.

l: endless torment, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 6
s: The lake of fire and brimstone is identified as endless torment.

l: the strait gate, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 6
s: My brethren are urged to enter in at the strait gate.

l: the way which is narrow, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 6
s: My brethren are urged to continue in the way which is narrow until they obtain eternal life.

l: eternal life, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 6
s: Eternal life is obtained by continuing in the way which is narrow after entering in at the strait gate.

l: the bar of God, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 6
s: The bar of God is where the speaker will meet my brethren. It is a pleasing bar to some, but it strikes the wicked with awful dread and fear.

l: The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 7
s: Sherem preaches among the people of Nephi that there is no Christ and seeks to overthrow the doctrine of Christ, but Jacob confounds him through the power of the Lord and testimony of the scriptures. Sherem asks for a sign, is struck by the power of the Lord, and later confesses before the people that he was deceived by the devil and that Christ, the power of the Holy Ghost, and the ministering of angels are real. After Sherem dies, the people witness these events, are overcome by the power of God, and peace and the love of God are restored among them. The people of Nephi search the scriptures, defend themselves against the Lamanites, and Jacob gives the plates to Enos as he concludes his record.

l: Sherem, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 7
s: Sherem preaches that there is no Christ and uses flattering speech to lead many people away and overthrow the doctrine of Christ. He contends with Jacob, asks for a sign, is struck by the power of the Lord, and later confesses before the people that he was deceived by the devil.

l: Jacob, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 7
s: Jacob testifies that Christ shall come, that the scriptures testify of Christ, and that an atonement is necessary. He confounds Sherem through the power of the Lord, prays that God’s will be done, and later gives the plates to his son Enos.

l: Christ, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 7
s: Christ is the subject of Sherem’s denial and Jacob’s testimony. Sherem later confesses Christ before the people, and Jacob declares that Christ shall come and that the prophets testified of him.

l: God, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 7
s: God pours his Spirit into Jacob’s soul, gives him power to confound Sherem, and answers Jacob’s prayer. Sherem confesses that he lied unto God, and the power of God comes upon the multitude after Sherem’s death.

l: the Holy Ghost, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 7
s: The Holy Ghost makes the truth of Christ and the need for an atonement manifest to Jacob. Sherem later confesses the power of the Holy Ghost before the people.

l: the devil, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 7
s: The devil is identified as the source of Sherem’s flattering speech and as the power by which Sherem was deceived. Sherem confesses that he had been deceived by the power of the devil.

l: people of Nephi, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 7
s: The people of Nephi are influenced by Sherem, then gather to hear his final speech and witness his death. They search the scriptures, reject his words, fortify against the Lamanites, and become conquerors of their enemies.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 7
s: The Lamanites delight in wars and bloodshed, maintain an eternal hatred against the people of Nephi, and continually seek to destroy them. Attempts to restore them to the knowledge of the truth are vain in this unit.

l: doctrine of Christ, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 7
s: The doctrine of Christ is preached by Jacob and opposed by Sherem. Sherem seeks to overthrow it by declaring that there should be no Christ.

l: law of Moses, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 7
s: Sherem claims that the law of Moses is the right way and accuses Jacob of converting it into worship of a being who shall come many hundred years later. Jacob answers that the scriptures testify of Christ.

l: scriptures, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 7
s: Jacob says that the scriptures truly testify of Christ and that all the prophets spoke concerning him. After Sherem’s death, the people search the scriptures and no longer hearken to Sherem’s words.

l: atonement of Christ, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 7
s: Jacob declares that if no atonement were made, all mankind must be lost. His testimony of the atonement is made manifest to him by the power of the Holy Ghost.

l: faith in Christ, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 7
s: Jacob has faith in Christ who should come, based on revelations, visions of angels, and the voice of the Lord. Sherem seeks to shake Jacob from this faith but cannot do so.

l: Sherem's death, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 7
s: After being struck by the power of the Lord, Sherem is nourished for many days and asks the people to gather so he can speak before he dies. He gives up the ghost after confessing the Christ and acknowledging his deception.

l: Sherem's confession, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 7
s: Sherem confesses before the people that he denied Christ, lied unto God, and had been deceived by the power of the devil. He also confesses Christ, the power of the Holy Ghost, and the ministering of angels.

l: peace and restoration, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi, Chapter 7
s: After Sherem’s death and confession, peace and the love of God are restored among the people. They search the scriptures and no longer listen to the words of Sherem.

l: The Book of Enos, The Book of Enos, The Book of Enos / Chapter 1
s: Enos describes his struggle before God, receiving a remission of his sins through faith in Christ and then praying for the welfare of the Nephites and Lamanites. God promises to answer Enos according to his faith and covenants to preserve the records of the Nephites for the Lamanites in his own due time. Enos prophesies and testifies among the Nephites, whose efforts to restore the Lamanites to the true faith are unsuccessful. The chapter also describes the land, the peoples' conduct, wars between the Nephites and Lamanites, and Enos's expectation of rest with his Redeemer and of putting on immortality.

l: Enos, The Book of Enos, The Book of Enos / Chapter 1
s: Enos learns from his father, hunts in the forests, prays all day and night, receives a remission of his sins, and then prays for the Nephites and Lamanites. He obtains God's promise concerning the records of the Nephites, prophesies and testifies among the people of Nephi, and looks forward to resting with his Redeemer and putting on immortality.

l: Enos's father, The Book of Enos, The Book of Enos / Chapter 1
s: Enos's father was a just man who taught Enos in his language and in the nurture and admonition of the Lord. He and Enos's other fathers had required God to preserve the records, according to their faith.

l: God, The Book of Enos, The Book of Enos / Chapter 1
s: God forgives Enos's sins, explains that his faith in Christ has made him whole, and promises to answer his desires. God gives the Nephites the land, preserves the records according to his covenant, and judges the peoples according to their diligence and iniquity.

l: Christ, The Book of Enos, The Book of Enos / Chapter 1
s: Christ is the one in whom Enos has faith, although Enos has not yet heard or seen him. Christ will manifest himself in the flesh many years later.

l: Nephites, The Book of Enos, The Book of Enos / Chapter 1
s: The Nephites seek to restore the Lamanites to the true faith, but their efforts are vain because the Lamanites' hatred is fixed. The Nephites till the land, raise crops and animals, have many prophets, and are kept from destruction by exceedingly plain preaching and prophesying.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Enos, The Book of Enos / Chapter 1
s: The Lamanites are not destroyed, and Enos prays that they may someday receive the records of the Nephites and be brought unto salvation. Their hatred is fixed, they are described as wild and ferocious, and they continually seek to destroy the Nephites.

l: the land, The Book of Enos, The Book of Enos / Chapter 1
s: God has given the land to the Nephites, and it is a holy land. God does not curse it except for the cause of iniquity.

l: records of the Nephites, The Book of Enos, The Book of Enos / Chapter 1
s: Enos prays that the records of the Nephites will be preserved if his people are destroyed. God covenants to bring them forth to the Lamanites in his own due time.

l: the words of Enos's father, The Book of Enos, The Book of Enos / Chapter 1
s: The words Enos had often heard his father speak concerning eternal life and the joy of the saints sink deep into Enos's heart and lead him to hunger spiritually.

l: eternal life, The Book of Enos, The Book of Enos / Chapter 1
s: Enos's father taught him about eternal life, and those words help awaken Enos's desire for God.

l: sin, The Book of Enos, The Book of Enos / Chapter 1
s: Enos struggles before God for a remission of his sins, and his guilt is swept away after God forgives him.

l: faith, The Book of Enos, The Book of Enos / Chapter 1
s: Enos receives forgiveness because of his faith in Christ. His faith becomes unshaken, and God grants his desires and promises to preserve the records because of his faith.

l: prayer, The Book of Enos, The Book of Enos / Chapter 1
s: Enos kneels before his Maker and cries unto God in mighty prayer and supplication all day and into the night. He later prays and labors for the Nephites, the Lamanites, and the preservation of the records.

l: remission of sins, The Book of Enos, The Book of Enos / Chapter 1
s: Enos receives a remission of his sins after wrestling before God in prayer. God tells him that this occurs because of his faith in Christ.

l: forgiveness of sins, The Book of Enos, The Book of Enos / Chapter 1
s: God tells Enos that his sins are forgiven, and Enos knows that God cannot lie, so his guilt is swept away.

l: God's covenant, The Book of Enos, The Book of Enos / Chapter 1
s: God covenants with Enos that he will bring the records of the Nephites to the Lamanites in his own due time. Enos knows this will happen according to the covenant.

l: God's commandments, The Book of Enos, The Book of Enos / Chapter 1
s: God will visit the Nephites according to their diligence in keeping his commandments. Their transgressions will be brought down with sorrow upon their own heads.

l: salvation, The Book of Enos, The Book of Enos / Chapter 1
s: Enos desires that the records of the Nephites might be brought to the Lamanites so that perhaps they may be brought unto salvation.

l: wars between the Nephites and Lamanites, The Book of Enos, The Book of Enos / Chapter 1
s: Enos sees wars between the Nephites and Lamanites during the course of his days.

l: preaching and prophesying, The Book of Enos, The Book of Enos / Chapter 1
s: Enos preaches and prophesies according to the truth in Christ and declares the word throughout his days. Among the Nephites, exceedingly harsh preaching and prophesying about war, destruction, death, eternity, judgment, and God's power are needed to keep them from destruction.

l: immortality, The Book of Enos, The Book of Enos / Chapter 1
s: Enos rejoices in the day when his mortal body will put on immortality and he will stand before God and see his face with pleasure.

l: The Book of Jarom, The Book of Jarom, The Book of Jarom / Chapter 1
s: Jarom writes a brief record on small plates according to the commandment of his father, Enos, for the benefit of the Lamanites. The Nephites grow strong, keep the law of Moses and the commandments, defend themselves against the Lamanites, and become prosperous in the land. Prophets, priests, and teachers warn the people, teach the law of Moses, and persuade them to look forward to the Messiah, helping prevent their destruction. Jarom records years of wars, contentions, and dissensions before delivering the plates to his son Omni.

l: Jarom, The Book of Jarom, The Book of Jarom / Chapter 1
s: Jarom writes a brief record according to the commandment of his father, Enos. He does not write his prophesying or revelations, refers readers to the other plates of Nephi for records of wars, and delivers his plates to his son Omni.

l: Messiah, The Book of Jarom, The Book of Jarom / Chapter 1
s: The prophets, priests, and teachers persuade the people to look forward unto the Messiah and believe in him to come as though he already was.

l: Lord, The Book of Jarom, The Book of Jarom / Chapter 1
s: The Lord is the one whom the Nephites' kings and leaders serve in faith. The people observe the sabbath day holy unto the Lord, and the Lord's prophets threaten the people according to the word of God.

l: God, The Book of Jarom, The Book of Jarom / Chapter 1
s: God's word warns that the Nephites will be destroyed from the face of the land if they do not keep the commandments and fall into transgression.

l: Nephites, The Book of Jarom, The Book of Jarom / Chapter 1
s: The Nephites become strong, multiply, spread across the land, and grow rich in precious materials and workmanship. Their kings and leaders teach them the ways of the Lord, and they withstand and drive away the Lamanites.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Jarom, The Book of Jarom / Chapter 1
s: The Lamanites are more numerous than the Nephites, love murder, and drink the blood of beasts. They come many times against the Nephites in battle but do not prosper against them.

l: prophets, The Book of Jarom, The Book of Jarom / Chapter 1
s: The prophets warn the people of Nephi that transgression will lead to destruction. They labor diligently with priests and teachers to teach the law of Moses, testify of the Messiah, and stir the people to repentance.

l: land, The Book of Jarom, The Book of Jarom / Chapter 1
s: The Nephites are not swept from the face of the land because of God's mercy. They spread across the land, fortify their cities and places of inheritance, and are warned that disobedience would bring destruction from it.

l: plates, The Book of Jarom, The Book of Jarom / Chapter 1
s: Jarom writes on small plates so the genealogy may be kept and for the benefit of the Lamanites. He says the other plates of Nephi contain records of the wars and delivers his plates to Omni.

l: plan of salvation, The Book of Jarom, The Book of Jarom / Chapter 1
s: Jarom says that his fathers have revealed the plan of salvation, and he considers this sufficient to write about.

l: law of Moses, The Book of Jarom, The Book of Jarom / Chapter 1
s: The Nephites observe the law of Moses, and the prophets, priests, and teachers teach both the law and the intent for which it was given.

l: commandments, The Book of Jarom, The Book of Jarom / Chapter 1
s: The Nephites are taught that keeping the commandments brings prosperity in the land. They are warned that failing to keep them and falling into transgression will result in destruction.

l: wars, The Book of Jarom, The Book of Jarom / Chapter 1
s: Jarom says that much of the time through two hundred and thirty-eight years was occupied by wars, contentions, and dissensions. He directs readers to the other plates of Nephi for records of the wars.

l: battles, The Book of Jarom, The Book of Jarom / Chapter 1
s: The Lamanites come many times against the Nephites to battle. The Nephites withstand them and sweep them away from their lands.

l: destruction, The Book of Jarom, The Book of Jarom / Chapter 1
s: The prophets warn that the people will be destroyed from the face of the land if they do not keep the commandments. The people's teaching and repentance keep them from being destroyed during this period.

l: repentance, The Book of Jarom, The Book of Jarom / Chapter 1
s: The prophets, priests, and teachers continually stir the people up unto repentance by pricking their hearts with the word.

l: The Book of Omni, The Book of Omni, The Book of Omni / Chapter 1
s: Omni, Amaron, Chemish, Abinadom, and Amaleki successively keep the plates and record warfare, judgments, transfers of the records, and teachings. Mosiah leads those who heed the Lord from the land of Nephi through the wilderness to the land of Zarahemla, where they discover and unite with the people of Zarahemla. The Lord preserves the righteous, gives Mosiah power to interpret engravings, and allows the Nephites to gain advantage over the Lamanites. Amaleki gives the plates to Benjamin and describes an unsuccessful attempt to return to the land of Nephi.

l: Omni, The Book of Omni, The Book of Omni / Chapter 1
s: Omni was commanded by his father Jarom to write on the plates. He fought with the sword to preserve the Nephites from the Lamanites, acknowledged that he was wicked and had not kept the Lord’s commandments as he should, and delivered the plates to his son Amaron.

l: Amaron, The Book of Omni, The Book of Omni / Chapter 1
s: Amaron wrote a few things in his father’s book. He recorded that after three hundred and twenty years the more wicked part of the Nephites had been destroyed, and he delivered the plates to his brother Chemish.

l: Chemish, The Book of Omni, The Book of Omni / Chapter 1
s: Chemish wrote a few things in the same book as his brother Amaron. He confirmed that Amaron wrote his final record with his own hand when he delivered the plates to him.

l: Abinadom, The Book of Omni, The Book of Omni / Chapter 1
s: Abinadom was the son of Chemish. He witnessed much war and contention between the Nephites and the Lamanites and killed many Lamanites with his sword in defense of his brethren.

l: Amaleki, The Book of Omni, The Book of Omni / Chapter 1
s: Amaleki was the son of Abinadom and wrote about Mosiah, Benjamin, the people of Zarahemla, and an attempted return to the land of Nephi. Having no seed and knowing Benjamin was just before the Lord, Amaleki delivered the plates to him and exhorted people to come unto God and Christ.

l: Mosiah, The Book of Omni, The Book of Omni / Chapter 1
s: Mosiah was warned by the Lord to flee the land of Nephi with those who would heed the Lord. He led them through the wilderness to the land of Zarahemla, became king after the people united, taught the people of Zarahemla his language, and interpreted engravings on a large stone by the gift and power of God.

l: Benjamin, The Book of Omni, The Book of Omni / Chapter 1
s: Benjamin was the son of Mosiah and reigned in his stead. Amaleki described him as a just man before the Lord and delivered the plates to him.

l: Zarahemla, The Book of Omni, The Book of Omni / Chapter 1
s: Zarahemla was associated with the people discovered by Mosiah. He rejoiced greatly when the Lord sent Mosiah’s people with the plates of brass and gave a genealogy of his fathers from memory.

l: the Lord, The Book of Omni, The Book of Omni / Chapter 1
s: The Lord warned Mosiah to flee the land of Nephi, led his people through the wilderness, and sent them to the people of Zarahemla with the plates of brass. The Lord brought judgment upon the wicked Nephites, spared the righteous, and gave Mosiah power to interpret engravings.

l: God, The Book of Omni, The Book of Omni / Chapter 1
s: God is identified as the source of all that is good, while evil comes from the devil. Mosiah interpreted the engravings by the gift and power of God, and Amaleki exhorted people to come unto God, the Holy One of Israel.

l: the Nephites, The Book of Omni, The Book of Omni / Chapter 1
s: The Nephites experienced seasons of peace, war, and bloodshed. The more wicked part of them was destroyed, while the righteous were spared, and under King Benjamin they gained much advantage over the Lamanites and drove them from the land of Zarahemla.

l: the Lamanites, The Book of Omni, The Book of Omni / Chapter 1
s: The Lamanites were enemies of the Nephites. Abinadom killed many of them, and the Nephites later gained much advantage over them and drove them from the land of Zarahemla.

l: the people of Zarahemla, The Book of Omni, The Book of Omni / Chapter 1
s: The people of Zarahemla were discovered by Mosiah’s people in the land of Zarahemla. They rejoiced at the arrival of Mosiah’s people, had come from Jerusalem in the time of Zedekiah, crossed the great waters, became numerous, suffered wars, lost their language and records, and united with Mosiah’s people.

l: the land of Nephi, The Book of Omni, The Book of Omni / Chapter 1
s: The land of Nephi was the place from which Mosiah was warned by the Lord to flee. A considerable number later attempted to return to it but were slain in the wilderness except for fifty, who returned to the land of Zarahemla.

l: the wilderness, The Book of Omni, The Book of Omni / Chapter 1
s: The wilderness was the route through which Mosiah’s people were led by the power of the Lord to the land of Zarahemla. It was also the place where the first attempted return to the land of Nephi ended in the deaths of all but fifty people.

l: the land of Zarahemla, The Book of Omni, The Book of Omni / Chapter 1
s: The land of Zarahemla was where Mosiah’s people arrived and discovered the people of Zarahemla. The two peoples united there, Mosiah became their king, and King Benjamin drove the Lamanites out of it.

l: the plates, The Book of Omni, The Book of Omni / Chapter 1
s: The plates preserved the genealogy and records of the people and were passed from Omni to Amaron, Chemish, Abinadom, and Amaleki. Amaleki delivered them to Benjamin when the plates were full.

l: the plates of brass, The Book of Omni, The Book of Omni / Chapter 1
s: The plates of brass were carried by Mosiah’s people to the people of Zarahemla. They contained the record of the Jews and were a cause of great rejoicing among the people of Zarahemla.

l: the record of this people, The Book of Omni, The Book of Omni / Chapter 1
s: The record of this people was engraved upon plates held by the kings according to the generations. Abinadom said that what was sufficient had been written and that he knew of no revelation or prophecy beyond what had been recorded.

l: genealogy, The Book of Omni, The Book of Omni / Chapter 1
s: Genealogy was preserved on the plates. Zarahemla gave a genealogy of his fathers from memory, and the record of it was written but not on the plates.

l: the commandments of the Lord, The Book of Omni, The Book of Omni / Chapter 1
s: The commandments of the Lord were not kept by Omni as he believed they should have been. The Lord’s judgment on the Nephites was tied to the warning that those who did not keep the commandments would not prosper in the land.

l: prophecy and revelation, The Book of Omni, The Book of Omni / Chapter 1
s: Prophecy and revelation were included among the good things Amaleki urged people to believe in. Abinadom said he knew of no revelation or prophecy save what had been written.

l: salvation, The Book of Omni, The Book of Omni / Chapter 1
s: Salvation was associated with coming unto Christ, the Holy One of Israel, and partaking of his salvation. Amaleki taught that those who continued in fasting and praying and endured to the end would be saved.

l: redemption, The Book of Omni, The Book of Omni / Chapter 1
s: Redemption was described as a power found in Christ. Amaleki urged people to come unto Christ and partake of the power of his redemption.

l: war and bloodshed, The Book of Omni, The Book of Omni / Chapter 1
s: War and bloodshed occurred repeatedly between the Nephites and the Lamanites. The unit records seasons of serious war, Abinadom’s killings, and a serious war during the reign of Benjamin.

l: the destruction of the Nephites, The Book of Omni, The Book of Omni / Chapter 1
s: The more wicked part of the Nephites was destroyed after three hundred and twenty years had passed. The Lord nevertheless spared the righteous so that they would not perish.

l: the exodus of Mosiah's people, The Book of Omni, The Book of Omni / Chapter 1
s: Mosiah’s people left the land of Nephi after Mosiah was warned by the Lord. Those who heeded the Lord were led through the wilderness by preaching, prophesying, continual admonition, and the power of the Lord’s arm to the land of Zarahemla.

l: the discovery of the people of Zarahemla, The Book of Omni, The Book of Omni / Chapter 1
s: Mosiah’s people discovered the people of Zarahemla in the land of Zarahemla. Mosiah learned that they had come from Jerusalem in the time of Zedekiah, crossed the great waters, and had no records with them.

l: the union of the people of Zarahemla and Mosiah, The Book of Omni, The Book of Omni / Chapter 1
s: The people of Zarahemla and Mosiah united together after Mosiah’s people taught them the language of Mosiah. Mosiah was appointed king over the united people.

l: the attempted return to the land of Nephi, The Book of Omni, The Book of Omni / Chapter 1
s: A large number of people attempted to return to the land of Nephi to possess the land of their inheritance. Their strong and stiffnecked leader caused contention, all but fifty were slain in the wilderness, and the survivors returned to the land of Zarahemla; another group later departed, including Amaleki’s brother, whose fate was unknown.

l: The Words of Mormon, The Words of Mormon, The Words of Mormon / Chapter 1
s: Mormon is about to deliver the record he has been making into the hands of his son Moroni after witnessing almost all the destruction of the Nephites. He finds plates containing an account from Jacob to the reign of king Benjamin and many of the words of Nephi, and he chooses to include them because of their prophecies concerning the coming of Christ. The records are preserved for a wise purpose, and Mormon prays that his brethren may return to the knowledge of God and the redemption of Christ. King Benjamin and the holy prophets establish peace after battles, contentions, false Christs, false prophets, and false teachers.

l: Mormon, The Words of Mormon, The Words of Mormon / Chapter 1
s: Mormon is about to deliver the record he has been making into the hands of his son Moroni. He has witnessed almost all the destruction of the Nephites, finds plates containing an account from Jacob to the reign of king Benjamin, and chooses to include them in his record.

l: Moroni, The Words of Mormon, The Words of Mormon / Chapter 1
s: Moroni is Mormon’s son and is to receive the record Mormon has been making. Mormon supposes that Moroni will witness the entire destruction of the Nephites, but prays that he may survive them and write concerning them and Christ.

l: Nephites, The Words of Mormon, The Words of Mormon / Chapter 1
s: The Nephites are Mormon’s people, and Mormon has witnessed almost all their destruction. Mormon prays that his brethren may once again become a delightsome people.

l: God, The Words of Mormon, The Words of Mormon / Chapter 1
s: God knows all things which are to come and works in Mormon according to his will. Mormon prays to God concerning his brethren and asks that the records be preserved.

l: Christ, The Words of Mormon, The Words of Mormon / Chapter 1
s: Christ is the subject of prophecies in the plates Mormon finds. Mormon hopes that Moroni may write concerning Christ, and he prays that his brethren may return to the redemption of Christ.

l: king Benjamin, The Words of Mormon, The Words of Mormon / Chapter 1
s: King Benjamin receives the plates from Amaleki, puts them with the other plates, and reigns over his people in righteousness. He gathers his armies against the Lamanites, fights with the sword of Laban, and, with the help of the holy prophets, establishes peace in the land.

l: Lamanites, The Words of Mormon, The Words of Mormon / Chapter 1
s: The Lamanites come down out of the land of Nephi to battle against king Benjamin’s people. King Benjamin and his armies contend against them, slay many thousands, and drive them out of all the lands of their inheritance.

l: record Mormon was making, The Words of Mormon, The Words of Mormon / Chapter 1
s: Mormon is about to deliver the record he has been making into the hands of Moroni. He finishes part of it from the plates of Nephi and says that he cannot write the hundredth part of the things of his people.

l: records, The Words of Mormon, The Words of Mormon / Chapter 1
s: Mormon searches among the records delivered into his hands and finds plates containing an account of prophets and many of the words of Nephi. The records are handed down from generation to generation, and Mormon prays that they will be preserved because great things are written upon them.

l: plates, The Words of Mormon, The Words of Mormon / Chapter 1
s: Mormon finds plates containing a small account of the prophets from Jacob down to the reign of king Benjamin and many of the words of Nephi. He chooses to take these plates and put them with the remainder of his record because they are choice to him and will be choice to his brethren.

l: plates of Nephi, The Words of Mormon, The Words of Mormon / Chapter 1
s: Mormon makes an abridgment from the plates of Nephi down to the reign of king Benjamin. He takes the remainder of his record from the plates of Nephi.

l: destruction of the Nephites, The Words of Mormon, The Words of Mormon / Chapter 1
s: Mormon has witnessed almost all the destruction of the Nephites. He supposes that Moroni will witness their entire destruction, and he prays that Moroni may survive them.

l: coming of Christ, The Words of Mormon, The Words of Mormon / Chapter 1
s: The plates please Mormon because they contain prophecies of the coming of Christ. Mormon says that many of these prophecies have been fulfilled and that the remaining things prophesied must come to pass.

l: reign of king Benjamin, The Words of Mormon, The Words of Mormon / Chapter 1
s: The account on the plates extends from Jacob down to the reign of king Benjamin. Mormon’s abridgment from the plates of Nephi also continues down to the reign of king Benjamin.

l: establishment of peace, The Words of Mormon, The Words of Mormon / Chapter 1
s: King Benjamin, with the assistance of the holy prophets among his people, establishes peace in the land. This follows battles against the Lamanites, false Christs, false prophets, false preachers and teachers, contentions, and dissensions.

l: prophecies, The Words of Mormon, The Words of Mormon / Chapter 1
s: The plates contain prophecies concerning the coming of Christ and concerning Mormon’s people down to that day and beyond it. Mormon says that many have been fulfilled and that those beyond that day must surely come to pass.

l: redemption of Christ, The Words of Mormon, The Words of Mormon / Chapter 1
s: Mormon prays that his brethren may once again come to the knowledge of the redemption of Christ. He hopes that they may once again become a delightsome people.

l: knowledge of God, The Words of Mormon, The Words of Mormon / Chapter 1
s: Mormon prays that his brethren may once again come to the knowledge of God. This prayer concerns their return to God and the redemption of Christ.

l: word of God, The Words of Mormon, The Words of Mormon / Chapter 1
s: The word of God is spoken with power and authority by holy men in the land. Records will be used to judge Mormon’s people and their brethren at the great and last day according to the word of God written upon them.

l: The Book of Mosiah, The Book of Mosiah, The Book of Mosiah / Chapter 1
s: King Benjamin teaches his sons, including Mosiah, Helorum, and Helaman, the language of their fathers, the records, and the commandments of God. He gives Mosiah charge to proclaim that the kingdom will be conferred upon him and that he will be a king and ruler over the people. King Benjamin also instructs Mosiah concerning the records, the sword of Laban, and the ball or director, and Mosiah proclaims the gathering of the people at the temple. The Lord has preserved the people when they keep the commandments, but transgression can cause them to become weak like the Lamanites.

l: king Benjamin, The Book of Mosiah, The Book of Mosiah / Chapter 1
s: King Benjamin has continual peace for the remainder of his days and teaches his sons concerning their fathers, the records, the commandments of God, and the Lord’s dealings. He grows old, gives Mosiah charge concerning the kingdom and its records, and plans to proclaim Mosiah as king and ruler.

l: Mosiah, The Book of Mosiah, The Book of Mosiah / Chapter 1
s: Mosiah is taught by king Benjamin and is brought before him to receive charge concerning the kingdom and its sacred objects. He is commanded to proclaim throughout the land that the people should gather, and he does as his father commanded.

l: Lord, The Book of Mosiah, The Book of Mosiah / Chapter 1
s: The Lord delivers prophecies and commandments to the fathers, preserves them by his power, and gives them the records and the ball or director. He promises prosperity when his commandments are kept and delivers the people up when they become wicked and transgress.

l: Zarahemla, The Book of Mosiah, The Book of Mosiah / Chapter 1
s: Zarahemla is the land where there is no more contention among the people who belonged to king Benjamin. Its people are included among those whom Mosiah proclaims should gather at the temple.

l: the people, The Book of Mosiah, The Book of Mosiah / Chapter 1
s: The people who belonged to king Benjamin have continual peace for the remainder of his days. They are part of the people whom Mosiah is commanded to gather.

l: the people of Zarahemla, The Book of Mosiah, The Book of Mosiah / Chapter 1
s: The people of Zarahemla are named among those whom Mosiah is commanded to gather. They are to gather at the temple to hear king Benjamin’s words.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Mosiah, The Book of Mosiah / Chapter 1
s: The Lamanites are described as brethren who know nothing concerning the records and mysteries of God or do not believe them when taught. They are also described as those among whom the people could become weak if they transgressed.

l: the plates of brass, The Book of Mosiah, The Book of Mosiah / Chapter 1
s: The plates of brass contain records and commandments and make it possible to read and understand the mysteries of God. King Benjamin teaches that without them the fathers would have suffered in ignorance and dwindled in unbelief.

l: the plates of Nephi, The Book of Mosiah, The Book of Mosiah / Chapter 1
s: The plates of Nephi contain the records and sayings of the fathers from the time they left Jerusalem until that time. King Benjamin says they are true and that their surety is known because they are before the people’s eyes.

l: the records, The Book of Mosiah, The Book of Mosiah / Chapter 1
s: The records are preserved by the hand of God and contain teachings, commandments, and the sayings of the fathers. King Benjamin commands his sons to search them diligently, and he gives charge concerning them to Mosiah.

l: the commandments of God, The Book of Mosiah, The Book of Mosiah / Chapter 1
s: The commandments of God are delivered through the records and are to be kept by the people. Keeping them brings prosperity according to the promises made to the fathers.

l: the mysteries of God, The Book of Mosiah, The Book of Mosiah / Chapter 1
s: The mysteries of God can be read and understood through the preserved records. King Benjamin teaches his sons that the plates help the people know these mysteries.

l: the kingdom, The Book of Mosiah, The Book of Mosiah / Chapter 1
s: The kingdom is to be conferred upon one of king Benjamin’s sons. King Benjamin gives Mosiah charge concerning all its affairs.

l: the name given to the people, The Book of Mosiah, The Book of Mosiah / Chapter 1
s: King Benjamin intends to give the people a name so they may be distinguished above the people brought out of the land of Jerusalem. He says the name will not be blotted out except through transgression.

l: the temple, The Book of Mosiah, The Book of Mosiah / Chapter 1
s: The temple is the place where the people are commanded to gather to hear the words king Benjamin will speak.

l: sin, The Book of Mosiah, The Book of Mosiah / Chapter 1
s: Transgression can cause the highly favored people of the Lord to become wicked and adulterous, lose the Lord’s preservation, and become weak like their brethren. It is also the condition through which the name given to the people may be blotted out.

l: the proclamation of Mosiah's kingship, The Book of Mosiah, The Book of Mosiah / Chapter 1
s: The proclamation of Mosiah's kingship is to be made throughout the land by Mosiah. It will announce that Mosiah is a king and ruler over the people whom the Lord has given them.

l: the gathering at the temple, The Book of Mosiah, The Book of Mosiah / Chapter 1
s: The gathering at the temple is commanded so the people of Zarahemla and the people of Mosiah may hear king Benjamin speak. Mosiah proclaims that the people should gather for this purpose.

l: Mosiah's succession, The Book of Mosiah, The Book of Mosiah / Chapter 1
s: The succession of Mosiah concerns king Benjamin’s intention to confer the kingdom upon Mosiah. Mosiah is to become a king and ruler over the people.

l: The Book of Mosiah, The Book of Mosiah, Chapter 2
s: The people gather at the temple to hear king Benjamin, who speaks from a tower because the multitude is too great for the temple. King Benjamin teaches that serving others is serving God, that all people are indebted to God, and that keeping the commandments brings prosperity and blessings. He announces that Mosiah is now king and warns the people against obeying the evil spirit, transgressing, and dying unrepentant. He describes the guilt and punishment of those who rebel against God and the never-ending happiness of those who remain faithful.

l: king Benjamin, The Book of Mosiah, Chapter 2
s: King Benjamin gathers the people so he can speak to them, teaches them about service, obedience, repentance, and accountability before God, and announces that he can no longer be their teacher or king. He declares that Mosiah is a king and ruler over the people and seeks to be blameless before God concerning them.

l: Mosiah (Benjamin's son), The Book of Mosiah, Chapter 2
s: Mosiah carries out what his father commanded and makes a proclamation throughout the land. King Benjamin declares that Mosiah is a king and ruler over the people and instructs them to keep his commandments and the commandments of God delivered through him.

l: Lord, The Book of Mosiah, Chapter 2
s: God brings the people out of Jerusalem, delivers them from enemies, gives them teachers and rulers, preserves and supports them, and grants them life and peace. He requires them to keep his commandments and blesses and prospers them when they do so.

l: the people, The Book of Mosiah, Chapter 2
s: The people gather throughout the land at the temple with their families, offer sacrifices, and listen to king Benjamin's words. They are taught that they are eternally indebted to God, should serve one another, and must keep the commandments.

l: Zarahemla, The Book of Mosiah, Chapter 2
s: Zarahemla is the land where the people have peace under the rule of a just king.

l: land, The Book of Mosiah, Chapter 2
s: The people multiply and wax great in the land. They are promised prosperity in the land if they keep the commandments, and protection from their enemies.

l: the temple, The Book of Mosiah, Chapter 2
s: The people gather at the temple and pitch their tents around it with their doors facing toward it. Because the multitude is too great to fit within its walls, a tower is erected so the people can hear king Benjamin.

l: tower near the temple, The Book of Mosiah, Chapter 2
s: A tower is erected because king Benjamin cannot teach the entire multitude within the temple walls. He speaks from the tower, and his words are written and sent to those who cannot hear him.

l: the commandments of God, The Book of Mosiah, Chapter 2
s: The commandments of God are to be kept in all things. Keeping them brings blessings, prosperity, and protection, while transgressing against them leads a person away from the Spirit of the Lord and into rebellion against God.

l: the evil spirit, The Book of Mosiah, Chapter 2
s: The evil spirit is one whom the people are warned not to obey. Those who listen to it and remain in their sins become enemies to righteousness and receive punishment.

l: Spirit of the Lord, The Book of Mosiah, Chapter 2
s: The Spirit of the Lord guides people in wisdom's paths so they may be blessed, prospered, and preserved. Transgression and rebellion can cause a person to withdraw from the Spirit so that it has no place in them.

l: divine justice, The Book of Mosiah, Chapter 2
s: Divine justice awakens the immortal soul of an unrepentant enemy of God to a lively sense of guilt. This produces shrinking from the Lord's presence and fills the person with guilt, pain, and anguish.

l: heaven, The Book of Mosiah, Chapter 2
s: Those who keep God's commandments faithfully to the end are received into heaven, where they may dwell with God in never-ending happiness.

l: the gathering at the temple, The Book of Mosiah, Chapter 2
s: The gathering brings the people and their families together to hear king Benjamin and to receive his teachings. King Benjamin also causes the gathering so he can declare his final instructions and be found blameless before God.

l: king Benjamin's speech, The Book of Mosiah, Chapter 2
s: King Benjamin's speech teaches that serving fellow beings is serving God, that people are indebted to God, and that obedience brings blessings. It also warns against rebellion, sin, and the evil spirit while describing the consequences of unrepentant transgression.

l: Mosiah's succession, The Book of Mosiah, Chapter 2
s: King Benjamin announces that his son Mosiah is a king and ruler over the people. He tells the people that they will prosper if they keep Mosiah's commandments and the commandments of God delivered by him.

l: service to one another, The Book of Mosiah, Chapter 2
s: Service to others is taught to be service to God. King Benjamin says that because he has labored to serve the people, they should likewise labor to serve one another.

l: sin, The Book of Mosiah, Chapter 2
s: Transgression against what has been taught withdraws a person from the Spirit of the Lord and constitutes open rebellion against God. An unrepentant person who remains an enemy to God dies in that condition and faces the consequences of guilt and anguish.

l: everlasting punishment, The Book of Mosiah, Chapter 2
s: Those who obey the evil spirit, remain in their sins, and die without repentance receive damnation and everlasting punishment. The final doom of an unrepentant enemy of God is described as never-ending torment.
